sources.name: THC Cannabis Encyclopedia Volume 13 — Terpenes, Volatiles, and Other Secondary Metabolites
sources.notes: Controls THC explanations, interpretation guardrails, cannabis-specific teaching language, and claims discipline.

sources.name: PubChem
sources.notes: Primary normalization source for CIDs, names, formulae, molecular weights, InChIKeys, SMILES, synonyms, and structure identifiers.

sources.name: COCONUT natural products database
sources.notes: Primary bulk natural-products feed for the global terpene/terpenoid registry. September 2026 CSV-lite release is versioned and ingested as source candidates; preserve upstream IDs/release and do not auto-promote candidates to reviewed THC records.

sources.name: Peer-reviewed cannabis chemistry and terpene-synthase literature
sources.notes: Stores sample context, analytical method, compound occurrence, TPS evidence, and study-level provenance.

sources.name: Qualified cannabis laboratory and published sample datasets
sources.notes: Never collapse source samples into a single permanent strain percentage. Preserve lab, date, units, method, and provenance.

sources.name: DTF Genetics breeding, phenotype, pedigree, and future COA records
sources.notes: Connect parent chemistry to measured offspring and selections. Predictions remain probabilistic until supported by offspring data.

sources.name: The phytochemical diversity of commercial Cannabis in the United States — published dataset
sources.notes: Published cleaned laboratory dataset spanning multiple U.S. testing labs. Preserve sample-level records and dataset-normalized strain_slug; do not turn cultivar labels into fixed chemistry values.

sources.name: Booth JK, Page JE, Bohlmann J. Terpene synthases from Cannabis sativa.
sources.notes: Primary functional characterization source for multiple Cannabis sativa terpene synthases. Table 2 and Fig. 4 are key gene-product evidence locations.

sources.name: Booth JK et al. Terpene Synthases and Terpene Variation in Cannabis sativa.
sources.notes: Expanded terpene synthase family and terpene variation reference for future gene/cultivar evidence.

sources.name: LOTUS Initiative / Natural Products Online
sources.notes: Secondary open natural-products occurrence source intended for cross-checking organism/occurrence evidence and expanding provenance. Do not merge identities by common name; use exact structure identifiers.

sources.name: Bueno J et al. The preservation and augmentation of volatile terpenes in cannabis inflorescence.
sources.notes: Cannabis inflorescence storage/packaging study using HS GC-MS. Preserve study-specific storage conditions and conflict-of-interest context.

sources.name: Kim YW et al. Safety evaluation and risk assessment of d-Limonene.
sources.notes: Toxicology/risk review for d-limonene. Use only for the exposure routes and endpoints discussed by the source; do not generalize to cannabis inhalation.

sources.name: Sköld M et al. Contact allergens formed on air exposure of linalool.
sources.notes: Experimental autoxidation and sensitization work on linalool and oxidation products; includes chromatographic/NMR identification and LLNA testing.

sources.name: Api AM et al. RIFM fragrance ingredient safety assessment, β-caryophyllene.
sources.notes: Fragrance-use safety assessment covering genotoxicity, repeated dose, reproductive, respiratory, phototoxicity/photoallergenicity, sensitization, and environmental endpoints.

sources.name: Surendran S et al. Myrcene—What Are the Potential Health Benefits of This Flavouring and Aroma Agent?
sources.notes: Review of β-myrcene occurrence, biological research, and toxicological profile; explicitly notes limited human evidence for proposed biological effects.

sources.name: Botvid S et al. Ten Years of Patch Testing to Hydroperoxides of Limonene and Linalool.
sources.notes: Human patch-testing dataset focused on hydroperoxides formed by autoxidation of limonene and linalool. Applies to contact-allergy context, not general cannabis exposure.
